To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) Ang‐1 and/or Ang‐2 expression is increased in colon carcinoma, and (ii) the increase in Ang‐1 and in Ang‐2 is not associated with a change in the ratio of Ang‐1 to Ang‐2 expression.

(1) Ang‐1 and ‐2 are differentially expressed in colon carcinoma; (2) the Ang‐1/Ang‐2 ratio is decreased in colon carcinoma compared with normal mucosa; (3) the Ang‐2/Ang‐1 ratio correlates with microvascular density and is a predictor of disease outcome; and (4) Ang‐1 is expressed by tumor‐associated macrophages, whereas Ang‐2 is expressed by tumor cells.
Ang‐1 expression is decreased in colon carcinoma and that this decrease is associated with an increase in Ang2 expression, resulting in an imbalance of angiogenic factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential expression of Ang‐1, Ang‐2 and Tie‐2 in colon cancer.
the role of angiopoietins in the regulation of angiogenesis.
the study of the expression of the angiopoietins in human colon carcinoma, and its correlation with the clinicopathological features of the tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
angiopoietins are differentially expressed in colon carcinoma, with a net gain in expression of Ang‐2.
Ang‐1 and ‐2 are differentially expressed in colon carcinoma.
Ang‐1 is downregulated and Ang‐2 upregulated in colon carcinoma and that the Ang‐1 to Ang‐2 ratio is significantly reduced in colon carcinoma compared with normal mucosa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ang‐1/Ang‐2 ratio is decreased in colon carcinoma, and this imbalance may contribute to the angiogenesis observed in this tumor type.
the imbalance of angiopoietins is a critical step in colon carcinogenesis.
the balance between Ang‐1 and ‐2 is shifted toward the proangiogenic Ang‐2 in colon cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of Ang‐2 and Ang‐1 in colon carcinoma is not the same in all tumor types.
the balance of Ang‐1 to Ang‐2 in tumor tissue is important for tumor progression and that Ang‐1 is a negative regulator of tumor growth.
the Ang/Tie‐2 axis is a key regulator of angiogenesis and that the balance of Ang‐1 to Ang‐2 is critical in maintaining vascular integrity.
